title: The Letters of Sandpiper Point Anew
premise: Jude Brightwater built a career planning other people's perfect days after her own engagement collapsed, and she's sworn off love until the lease on Sandpiper Point's beloved bakery—her late grandmother's legacy—forces her back to the coastal town she fled. Stranded by a snowstorm with Theo Marchetti, the rival planner who stole her biggest client and the man she almost loved a decade ago, Jude must co-plan one impossible wedding to save both their reputations. As the bakery's final lease deadline looms, Jude discovers her grandmother left the property to whoever can prove they'll stay, forcing her to choose between the career that saved her and a future she stopped believing she deserved. She signs nothing, keeps the bakery, and chooses Theo—not because the storm stranded them, but because staying was finally her own idea.
about_author: Jonah Montrose is the pen name of a former event coordinator who spent seven years watching strangers fall in love at other people's weddings before trading clipboards for manuscripts. They write from a rented cottage on the Atlantic coast, where the bakery down the road inspired everything.

chapters.title: The Last Perfect Day
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At a flawless Nantucket wedding, Jude orchestrates joy she no longer feels, then learns the Sandpiper Point bakery lease expires in ninety days. The emotional beat is numb competence cracking into dread as her past literally mails itself back to her.

chapters.title: Flour and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. She returns to Sandpiper Point to assess the bakery, finding her grandmother's recipe cards and an unfamiliar lawyer's letter about inheritance conditions. The beat is grief sharpening into suspicion: why would Gran leave strings attached?

chapters.title: The Rival at the Door
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives in town scouting venues for the Meridian Hotel account—and discovers Jude Brightwater, the planner whose client he poached, standing in his way. The beat is wary recognition laced with old guilt he's never admitted aloud.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Over hostile coffee, Jude and Theo discover they're both bidding for the same high-profile wedding that could save their careers. The beat is competitive fire masking attraction neither will name.

chapters.title: What the Storm Decided
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A freak October nor'easter strands them together in the shuttered bakery above the shop, power out, roads closed. The beat is forced proximity dissolving armor—one candlelit hour of honesty about the mistake of their twenties.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago, Briefly
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Trapped by snow, Theo confesses what really happened the night he left: he chose the job over her and has regretted it in every quiet moment since. The beat is raw vulnerability met with Jude's careful silence.

chapters.title: The Client Who Wants Everything
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Roads clear; the bride, Camille Voss, demands both planners co-lead or loses the wedding entirely. The beat is trapped ambition—Jude accepts for the money that might save the bakery lease.

chapters.title: Recipe Card Diplomacy
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Baking fails and flour fights in the test kitchen force collaboration; Theo realizes Jude's grandmother's recipes are the wedding menu's missing heart. The beat is reluctant admiration turning warm.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The inheritance clause surfaces: the bakery goes to whichever heir proves commitment to Sandpiper Point—and Jude's estranged cousin Delia is competing. The beat is betrayal compounding pressure as family becomes another rival.

chapters.title: Camille's Impossible List
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Camille escalates demands—a winter garden, a live orchestra, a venue that doesn't exist—threatening both planners' careers. The beat is shared panic forging real partnership over takeout containers at midnight.

chapters.title: Almost, Again
chapters.summary: Dual POV. After a successful vendor meeting, a near-kiss in the empty greenhouse is interrupted by Delia's arrival and a pointed phone call from Jude's ex-fiancé. The beat is hope yanked backward by every ghost she's kept.

chapters.title: The Ex-Fiancé's Offer
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Marcus returns offering to buy out the bakery lease—if Jude comes back to the city and the life she escaped. The beat is temptation dressed as rescue, and the horror of realizing how easily she almost says yes.

chapters.title: Delia's Version of Home
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Delia pitches the town council a boutique hotel conversion, winning public sympathy while Jude plans Camille's wedding. The beat is injustice and Jude's quiet fury at being painted the absentee granddaughter.

chapters.title: Snowmelt
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A thaw weekend, a walk on the cold beach, and finally the kiss ten years overdue. The beat is surrender—but Jude pulls away after, terrified that wanting something is how she loses it.

chapters.title: The Sabotage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Camille's wedding flowers arrive frozen and the venue floods; evidence suggests deliberate sabotage aimed at discrediting Jude. The beat is protective rage as Theo realizes someone wants her to fail badly enough to leave.

chapters.title: Accusations in the Dark
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Suspicion falls on Theo—he had motive, access, and a history of taking what was hers. The beat is heartbreak repeating its oldest pattern as Jude chooses doubt over trust, exactly like before.

chapters.title: The Ledger Delia Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo uncovers Delia's forged documents and sabotage trail, confronting her alone. The beat is moral clarity at personal cost—he can clear Jude's name only by exposing his own past lie about the poached client.

chapters.title: Confession Before the Cake Tasting
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Theo confesses everything publicly; Jude must decide whether love against duty means forgiving the man who wronged her twice. The beat is fury, grief, and the first honest choice she's made in a decade.

chapters.title: The Wedding That Almost Wasn't
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Camille's wedding day arrives amid chaos; Jude and Theo pull off the impossible together, and watching two people choose each other, Jude finally believes in weddings again. The beat is catharsis—the career and the heart reconciling.

chapters.title: Lease Day
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The lease deadline: Marcus's check, Delia's hotel bid, and Gran's clause all converge. Jude refuses the buyout, presents her plan to stay and run the bakery, and wins the inheritance on her own terms. The beat is defiant self-possession.

chapters.title: What Stays
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo turns down the Meridian partnership and asks for a place in Sandpiper Point—not in her life, but beside it, letting her choose him freely. The beat is humility as the truest form of love.

chapters.title: Letters of Sandpiper Point
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. One year later: the bakery thrives, Gran's letters reveal she engineered everything hoping Jude would come home to herself first. The final beat is peace—love kept not in the past tense, but in present continuous.
